learningObjective: Diagnose memory-bandwidth-bound decode from profile data and identify effective vs ineffective mitigations.

canonicalClaims.claim: Batch-1 decode of a dense transformer is memory-bandwidth bound on weight reads; effective mitigations reduce weight bytes (quantization), amortize weight reads over batch (continuous batching), or eliminate launch overhead (CUDA Graphs).
conditions: Weight bytes >> KV bytes per step (typical for shorter context).
nonImplications: Does not imply mitigations preserve quality.
Does not imply low SM utilization is a bug — it is expected under bandwidth-bound.

misconceptions.claim: Low SM utilization indicates need for more compute.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It indicates memory-bandwidth bound behavior; compute is intentionally idle waiting on memory.

misconceptions.claim: INT4 quantization always speeds up decode by 4x.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Speedup depends on kernel availability and dequant overhead; typical is 2-3x on well-tuned stacks.

misconceptions.claim: Continuous batching alone eliminates memory-bandwidth bound behavior.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Batching raises intensity but eventually hits either compute-bound or a different bandwidth ceiling (KV).

implementationFacts: A100 HBM peak ~2 TB/s; H100 SXM ~3.3 TB/s.
INT4 dequant + FP16 matmul kernels (AWQ, GPTQ) are the standard batch-1 decode path.
performanceScenarios: Batch=1 decode of a 13B FP16 model near peak HBM gives ~14-15 ms/token on A100; INT4 can reach ~5-7 ms/token.
